sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: George Galloway (born 16 August 1954) is a British politician, broadcaster, and writer.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He has been leader of the Workers Party of Britain since he founded it in 2019, and is a former leader of the Respect Party.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Until 2003, he was a member of the Labour Party.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: From 1987 to 2010, from 2012 to 2015, and briefly in 2024, Galloway served as Member of Parliament (MP) for five different constituencies.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: As of 2026, he is living in "self-imposed exile" in Russia.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Galloway was born in Dundee, Scotland.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: After becoming the youngest ever chair of the Scottish Labour Party in 1981, he was general secretary of the charity War on Want from 1983 until his election as MP for Glasgow Hillhead at the 1987 general election; he was re-elected three times.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: The Labour Party expelled him in 2003 due to comments he made in opposition to the invasion of Iraq.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Galloway joined the Respect Party in 2004, and was its leader from 2013 to 2016.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He was elected as MP for Bethnal Green and Bow at the 2005 general election.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: After losing in the neighbouring constituency of Poplar and Limehouse at the 2010 general election, he regained a parliamentary seat at the 2012 Bradford West by-election, only to lose it at the 2015 general election.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He unsuccessfully stood as an independent candidate at the 2017 and 2019 general elections.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Galloway then founded the Workers Party of Britain, and stood unsuccessfully for the party at the 2021 Batley and Spen by-election.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Galloway won the 2024 Rochdale by-election.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He lost the seat at the 2024 general election.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Galloway describes himself as both a socialist and socially conservative.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He travelled to Ba'athist Iraq to meet government officials in the 1990s, and caused controversy for praising Saddam Hussein at a 1994 meeting, which he denied.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Galloway founded the Mariam Appeal in 1998 to campaign against sanctions on Iraq.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Galloway was accused of receiving illicit payments from Iraq's government, partly from money diverted from the United Nations' Oil-for-Food Program, defending himself at a 2005 United States Senate hearing.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: A staunch opponent of Israel and of Zionism, he supports the Palestinians in the Israeli–Palestinian conflict and was involved in the 2009 Viva Palestina aid convoys to the Gaza Strip.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He supported Jeremy Corbyn in his leadership of the Labour Party.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: In 2016 he campaigned for the UK to leave the European Union, later supporting Nigel Farage's Brexit Party at the 2019 European Parliament election.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He opposes Scottish independence, and founded the British unionist alliance All for Unity, which received 0.9 per cent of votes at the 2021 Scottish Parliament election.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Galloway has supported the Russian invasion of Ukraine and blamed it on the West.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Galloway hosted the TalkRadio show The Mother of All Talk Shows from 2006 to 2010 and from 2016 until his dismissal in 2019.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He then moved the show to social media platforms.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He was a presenter on Russian state media outlet RT from 2013 to 2022, and was a presenter on Iranian state media outlet Press TV.

sentences.section: Background and education
sentences.text: Galloway was born in Dundee, Scotland on 16 August 1954, to George Galloway Sr., a Scottish trade unionist, and Sheila O'Reilly, a Scot of Irish descent.

sentences.section: Background and education
sentences.text: Initially raised in Lochee, Dundee, he has described himself as "born in an attic in a slum tenement in the Irish quarter of Dundee, which is known as Tipperary".

sentences.section: Background and education
sentences.text: His father began as an electrician, before studying a degree to become an electromechanical engineer at NCR.

sentences.section: Background and education
sentences.text: After being made redundant, he retrained as a teacher.

sentences.section: Background and education
sentences.text: His mother was a cleaner, and then a factory worker.

sentences.section: Background and education
sentences.text: According to Galloway, his father was patriotic, while his mother had Irish nationalist sympathies, and was critical of perceived British pretensions in the world.

sentences.section: Background and education
sentences.text: He took his mother's side in arguments, and has been a long-time supporter of Sinn Féin and Irish reunification.

sentences.section: Background and education
sentences.text: David Morley, his biographer, has written that people who knew both father and son have said that they had Marxist opinions common in the local Labour Party movement of the time.

sentences.section: Background and education
sentences.text: Galloway grew up in Charleston, Dundee, and attended Charleston Primary and then Harris Academy, in the city's West End, an academically selective and non-denominational state school, which became comprehensive in 1973.

sentences.section: Background and education
sentences.text: Galloway played for the school football team as well as for West End United U12s, Lochee Boys Club U16s and St Columba's U18s.

sentences.section: Background and education
sentences.text: In a 2016 New Internationalist interview, Galloway speculated that an incident of sexual abuse from a colonel, which he suffered when he was 12, caused a "lifelong fear of being gay and this led me into ostentatious, rapacious heterosexual promiscuity".

sentences.section: Background and education
sentences.text: According to Galloway, he grew a moustache at the age of 15, and refused to shave it off when his headmaster objected.

sentences.section: Background and education
sentences.text: He decided, at the age of 18, never to drink alcohol; the reason was originally derived from comments by his father, and he has described alcohol as having a "very deleterious effect on people".

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: Galloway joined the Labour Party Young Socialists aged 13, having falsely claimed to have been 15, and was still a teenager when he became secretary of the Dundee Labour Party.

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: Galloway became vice-chairman of the Labour Party in the City of Dundee and a member of the Scottish Executive Committee in 1975.

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: On 5 May 1977, he contested his first election campaign in the Scottish district elections, but failed to hold the safe Labour Gillburn ward in Dundee, being defeated by the independent Bunty Turley.

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: He became the secretary organiser of the Dundee Labour Party in 1977, and at 26, was the youngest ever chairman of the Scottish Labour Party in March 1981, a post he held for a year, after holding the vice-chairman post over the previous year.

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: After a trip to Beirut, Lebanon, during 1977, Galloway became a supporter of Palestine, stating during his libel case against The Daily Telegraph in 2004 that "barely a week after my return I made a pledge, in the Tavern Bar in Dundee's Hawkhill District, to devote the rest of my life to the Palestinian and Arab cause."

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: He supported Dundee City Council when it flew the Palestinian flag over the City Chambers building, and was involved in the twinning of Dundee with the Palestinian West Bank town of Nablus in 1980.

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: In late 1981, in an interview for the Scottish Marxist, Galloway supported the affiliation of the Communist Party of Great Britain (CPGB) to the Labour Party, in the same way as the Fabian Society does.

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: Believing that a deficiency in political theory was being filled by the entryist infiltration of the party by the Trotskyists (such as the Militant tendency), he thought the problem was better resolved by communist thinking from members of the CPGB.

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: (He was later opposed to the expulsion of members of Militant.)

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: In response, Denis Healey, Deputy Leader of the Labour Party, tried and failed to remove Galloway from the list of prospective parliamentary candidates.

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: Healey lost his motion by 13 votes to five.

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: Galloway once quipped that, to overcome a £1.5 million deficit which had arisen in Dundee's city budget, he, Ernie Ross, and leading councillors should be placed in the stocks in the city square: "We would allow people to throw buckets of water over us at 20p a time."

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: In 1983, Galloway attempted to stand for the safe Labour seat of Rhondda after the Welsh Transport and General Workers' Union and the National Union of Miners had both nominated him to succeed Alec Jones, who had died.

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: He hoped to be selected in the newly created seat of Dunfermline East, where no incumbent was standing.

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: Galloway failed to be selected for either seat, with Rhondda selecting Allan Rogers, and Dunfermline East selecting future Chancellor of the Exchequer and later Prime Minister, Gordon Brown.

sentences.section: Labour Party organiser
sentences.text: Standing as a candidate for a place on the Labour Party National Executive Committee in 1986, in a large field of 18 candidates, Galloway finished in 16th place.

sentences.section: War on Want
sentences.text: From November 1983 to 1987, Galloway was the general secretary of War on Want, a British charity campaigning against poverty worldwide.

sentences.section: War on Want
sentences.text: In this post he travelled widely, and wrote eye-witness accounts of the famine in Eritrea in 1985 which were published in The Sunday Times and The Spectator.

sentences.section: War on Want
sentences.text: His deputy at the charity, Simon Stocker, recalled: "If you went into a fight with George, you knew you would never walk out with a win."

sentences.section: War on Want
sentences.text: On 28 October 1986, the Daily Mirror, in a front-page story by Alastair Campbell, alleged Galloway had spent £20,000 in expenses and had been "enjoying a life of luxury".

sentences.section: War on Want
sentences.text: An internal investigation, and later, an independent auditor, both cleared him of the accusation of any misuse of funds, although he did repay £1,720 in contested expenses.

sentences.section: War on Want
sentences.text: The official history of War on Want comments about Galloway that "even though the problems were not all of his own making, his way of dealing with them heightened tensions".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: At the 1987 general election, Galloway was elected as the MP for Glasgow Hillhead gaining the seat for Labour from the SDP defeating Roy Jenkins with a majority of 3,251 votes.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Although known for his left-wing political views, Galloway was never a member of the Campaign Group.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In September 1987, Galloway was asked by a journalist about his relationship to a woman during the 1986 War on Want conference on the Greek island of Mykonos.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway admitted having an extra-marital affair, saying:I travelled to, and spent time in, Greece with lots of people, many of whom were women, some of whom were known carnally to me.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: I actually had sexual intercourse with some of the people in Greece.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: And if the British public and BBC Scotland think that's of interest they are welcome to broadcast it.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: As a result, Galloway made front-page headlines in the tabloid press at the time.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He and his first wife separated that year.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In February 1988, the executive committee of his constituency Labour Party passed a vote of no confidence in him by 15 to 8. The constituency's general management committee voted 54-to-44 in favour of the motion a fortnight later on 22 February, although just three of the 25 members in the trade union section supported it.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway gained re-selection when challenged by Trish Godman (wife of fellow MP Norman Godman) in June 1989, but failed to get a majority of the electoral college on the first ballot.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: This was the worst result for any sitting Labour MP who was reselected, but Galloway gained 62% in total in the final vote.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway assured his party there would be a "summer of peace and reconciliation" in his acceptance speech, but this did not happen.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Many members of the party who had supported Godman reportedly refused to work for Galloway in the next election, including Johann Lamont, who later became Leader of the Scottish Labour Party in 2011.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The following August, 13 of the 26 members of the constituency party's executive committee resigned, including Lamont.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: According to her, Galloway "has done nothing to build bridges with the Members of the Executive [Committee of the Constituency Labour Party] who opposed his selection."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: She told a journalist from The Guardian: "The quarrel we have is all about accountability, and democracy... working in harmony, rather than any personal matters."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The Labour Party leadership election in 1992 saw Galloway voting for the eventually successful candidates, John Smith for leader and Margaret Beckett as deputy leader.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In 1994, after Smith died, Galloway declined to cast a vote in the leadership election (one of only three MPs to do so).

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In a debate with the leader of the Scottish National Party, Alex Salmond, Galloway responded to one of Salmond's jibes against Labour by declaring "I don't give a fuck what Tony Blair thinks".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In 1997, Galloway's Glasgow Hillhead constituency was abolished and, although facing a challenge for the Labour nomination as the candidate for Glasgow Kelvin at the 1997 general election, Galloway defeated Shiona Waldron.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He was unchallenged for the nomination for the 2001 general election.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He was elected with majorities of 16,643 and 12,014 votes respectively.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: During the period he was Labour MP for Glasgow Kelvin, from 1997 to 2003, he voted against the whip 32 times, five votes out of 665 (0.8%) in the 1997–2001 parliament and the majority (27 votes out of 209 or 12.9%) in the period from the 2001 election until his expulsion from the Labour Party.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He was one of several politicians arrested in February 2001 during a protest at the Faslane nuclear base in Scotland, which led to him being convicted of a breach of the peace and fined £180.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In May 2002, he was among the 72 MPs who signed The Guardian'''s campaign to repeal the Act of Settlement 1701, alongside the Archbishop of York David Hope and several non-Anglican religious leaders.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Writing for The Observer in April 2003, David Aaronovitch speculated that Galloway's support for Ba'athist Iraq and Saddam Hussein may have been based on "the belief that my enemy's enemy is my friend.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Or, in the context of the modern world, any anti-American will do.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: When Iraq stopped being a friend of the West it became a friend of George's." According to Tam Dalyell, Galloway had been the "only one MP that I can recollect making speeches about human rights in Iraq" in the House of Commons.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway opposed the 1991 Gulf War and was critical of the effect that the subsequent sanctions had on the people of Iraq.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In January 1994, Galloway faced some of his strongest criticism for a Middle Eastern trip, during which he met Saddam Hussein.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: At his meeting with the Iraqi president, Galloway told Saddam Hussein,

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Your excellency, Mr President, I greet you in the name of the many thousands of people in Britain who stood against the tide and opposed the war ...

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: I greet you too in the name of the Palestinian people ...

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: I thought the president would appreciate knowing that even today, three years after the war, I still meet families who are calling their newborn sons Saddam ...

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Sir, I salute your courage, your strength, your indefatigability.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: And I want you to know that we are with you until victory, until victory, until Jerusalem (hatta al-nasr, hatta al-nasr, hatta al-Quds).

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: During Galloway's 2004 defamation case against the Daily Telegraph, the paper's defence Queen's Counsel accused Galloway of having "fawned over" Saddam during their meeting in 1994.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Labour leader John Smith said: "I deeply deplore the foolish statement made in Iraq by Mr. George Galloway.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In no way did he speak for the Labour Party and I wholly reject his comments".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway said that he was saluting the Iraqi people, rather than Saddam Hussein, and Galloway's friend Anas Altikriti observed that this is how it was translated for Saddam.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Shortly after his return, Galloway was given a "severe reprimand" and "final warning" by the Labour Chief Whip, Derek Foster.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway apologised for his conduct and undertook to follow future instruction from the whips.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: For his meeting with Saddam, Galloway was dubbed the "MP for Baghdad North".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: When he spoke before the U.S. Senate on 17 May 2005, Galloway said that he had "met Saddam Hussein exactly the same number of times as Donald Rumsfeld met him," but "The difference is Donald Rumsfeld met him to sell him guns ...

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: I met him to try to bring about an end to sanctions, suffering and war".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In the late 1990s, Galloway allegedly lost favour with Saddam Hussein after telling an interviewer that he supported the Iraqi people rather than their president.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In 1999, he met with Uday Hussein, Saddam's son.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 6 May 2002, Galloway met with Deputy Prime Minister Tariq Aziz in Baghdad on his second visit to Iraq that year, accompanied by the Labour peer Nicolas Rea and Labour MPs Kerry Pollard and Robert Wareing.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He was also scheduled to address a conference of solidarity with the Iraqi people.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: His party ran into the far-right Governor of Carinthia Jörg Haider returning from a meeting with Foreign Minister Naji Sabri.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway did not take his companions' suggestion to copy a scene from Casablanca by singing La Marsellaise in front of Haider.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 8 August 2002, two days after the Iraqi invitation to resume talks in Baghdad was rejected by the United Nations Security Council and against the mounting threat of US invasion, Galloway was received for the second time by Saddam Hussein.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Per Galloway's account, the meeting took place in a secret underground bunker near Baghdad.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: According to the Iraqi minutes from the meeting, examined in 2006 by the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards Sir Philip Mawer and dismissed by Galloway as forgeries, Tariq Aziz, Naji Sabri and Saddam's personal secretary Abid Hamid Mahmud were in attendance as Galloway offered Saddam British staff to launch an English-language Iraqi satellite television channel, and said oil prices were having an impact on the income of the Mariam Appeal.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In a radio interview given on the day following the discussion, Galloway said the Iraqi president was determined to show that his offer of readmitting the United Nations weapons inspectors into the country was sincere.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway said that the United States had nothing to lose by postponing its plans for invasion.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In an 11 August article for The Mail on Sunday, Galloway wrote that Saddam "clearly understood that Iraq has to be seen to go the extra diplomatic mile" and that he expressed fondness for "everything quintessentially British".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The piece was interpreted by the CNN as "the latest apparent charm offensive adopted by the Iraqi leader in the face of possible military action against it", and the British Foreign Office refused to consider the overtures.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 12 August, the Iraqi minister of information Muhammad Saeed al-Sahhaf rejected the return of the UN inspectors.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In January 2003, Galloway met with Saddam Hussein and Tariq Aziz once more.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: His claim that the encounter was held in an underground bunker was later contradicted by the Iraqi president's interpreter.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In 1998, Galloway founded the Mariam Appeal which was intended, according to its website's welcome page in 1999, "to campaign against sanctions on Iraq which are having disastrous effects on the ordinary people of Iraq".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The campaign was named after Mariam Hamza, a child flown by the fund from Iraq to Britain to receive treatment for leukaemia.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The intention was to raise awareness of the suffering and death of hundreds of thousands of other Iraqi children, due to poor health conditions and lack of suitable medicines and facilities, and to campaign for the lifting of the Iraq sanctions that many maintained were responsible for that situation.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In 1999, Galloway was criticised for spending Christmas in Iraq with Tariq Aziz, who was Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In a 17 May 2005 hearing of the United States Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, Galloway stated that he had many meetings with Aziz, and characterised their relationship as friendly.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He said at another occasion that he and Aziz met more than ten times.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: During the 2003 invasion of Iraq, the fund received scrutiny after a complaint that Galloway used some donated money to pay for his travel expenses.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He responded by stating that the expenses were incurred in his capacity as the appeal's chairman.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Although the Mariam Appeal was never a registered charity and never intended to be such, it was investigated by the Charity Commission.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The report of this year-long inquiry, published in June 2004, found that the Mariam Appeal was undertaking charitable work (and so ought to have registered with the commission), but did not substantiate allegations that any funds had been misused.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: It emerged some years later that Galloway had appealed in a letter dated 24 April 2003 to Lord Goldsmith, the Attorney-General, to stop the investigation into the Mariam Appeal.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: According to a report in The Times, after the letter was released under the Freedom of Information Act, Galloway falsely asserted that the appeal "received no money from Iraq".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: A further Charity Commission Report published on 7 June 2007 found that the appeal had received funds from Fawaz Zureikat that originated from the Oil-for-Food Programme, and concluded that,

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Although Mr Galloway, Mr Halford and Mr Al-Mukhtar have confirmed that they were unaware of the source of Mr Zureikat's donations, the Commission has concluded that the charity trustees should have made further enquiries when accepting such large single and cumulative donations to satisfy themselves as to their origin and legitimacy.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The Commission's conclusion is that the charity trustees did not properly discharge their duty of care as trustees to the Appeal in respect of these donations...

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The Commission is also concerned, having considered the totality of the evidence before it, that Mr Galloway may also have known of the connection between the Appeal and the Programme.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway, in response, stated: "I've always disputed the Commission's retrospective view that a campaign to win a change in national and international policy – a political campaign – was, in fact, a charity".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway became the vice-president of the Stop the War Coalition in 2001.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Actively involved, he often delivered speeches from StWC platforms at anti-war demonstrations.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: After permission for a rally in Hyde Park during the international anti-war protests on 15 February 2003 was initially refused, Galloway said the government had a choice between "half a million people at the rally or half a million people in a riot".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In I'm Not the Only One, Galloway wrote:

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The only war that can be fought against a superpower is a war of movement.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: I brought Tariq Aziz all the writings of Che Guevara and Mao Tse Tung on the arts of revolutionary war and he had them translated into Arabic.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Fight a war of movement, take the uniforms off, swim among the Iraqi people and whatever their views on the regime, they will undoubtedly provide deep aquifers of support for a patriotic resistance.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 20 March 2003, a coalition including the United Kingdom and United States invaded Ba'athist Iraq.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 28 March 2003, Galloway said in an interview with Abu Dhabi TV:Iraq is fighting for all the Arabs.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Why don't the Arabs do something for the Iraqis?

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Where are the Arab armies?

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: They [Tony Blair and George Bush] have lied to the British Air Force and Navy, when they said the battle of Iraq would be very quick and easy.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: They attacked Iraq like wolves.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: They attacked civilians.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: They encountered resistance from Iraqi forces and Iraqi people who are defending their dignity, religion and country ...

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: It is better for Blair and Bush to stop this crime and this catastrophe.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The best thing British troops can do is to refuse to obey illegal orders.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Labour leader Tony Blair said: "His comments were disgraceful and wrong.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The National Executive will deal with it".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Labour MP Tam Dalyell commented in Galloway's defence: "I think he is a deeply serious, committed politician and a man of great sincerity about the causes he takes up."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 6 May 2003, David Triesman, then general secretary of the Labour Party, suspended Galloway from holding office in the party pending a hearing on charges that he had violated the party's constitution by "bringing the Labour Party into disrepute through behaviour that is prejudicial or grossly detrimental to the Party."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway said he stood by every word of the Abu Dhabi interview.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The National Constitutional Committee, responsible for disciplinary matters in the Labour Party, held a hearing on 22 October 2003 to consider the charges, taking evidence from Galloway himself, from other party witnesses, viewing media interviews, and hearing character testimony from former cabinet minister Tony Benn, among others.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The following day, the committee unanimously found Galloway guilty of four of the five charges: inciting Arabs to fight British troops, inciting British troops to defy orders, inciting voters to reject Labour MPs, and threatening to stand against Labour.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway was expelled from the Labour Party.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway said after his expulsion: "This was a politically motivated kangaroo court whose verdict had been written in advance in the best tradition of political show trials".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He claimed that other MPs who opposed the war, such as Bob Marshall Andrews and Glenda Jackson, would soon be expelled, but no other MP was expelled from the Labour Party for opposing the Iraq War.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Ian McCartney, Labour Party chairman at the time, said Galloway was the only Labour MP who "incited foreign forces to rise up against British troops".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Tony Benn questioned why Galloway strove to remain in the Labour Party despite calling its leadership a "blood-splattered, lying, crooked group of war criminals".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Benn added, "It put me off George Galloway in a fairly fundamental way".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Following the 7 July 2005 London bombings, which killed 52 civilians, Galloway linked the attack to Western policies in the Middle East.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He said Tony Blair and George W. Bush had "far more blood on their hands" than the terrorists who carried out the bombings, and called President Bush the world's "biggest terrorist".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 22 April 2003, The Daily Telegraph published news articles and comment describing documents found by its reporter David Blair in the ruins of the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The documents purported to be records of meetings between Galloway and Iraqi intelligence agents, and they stated that he had received £375,000 per year from the proceeds of the United Nations (UN) Oil-for-Food Programme.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway denied the claims and pointed to the nature of the discovery within an unguarded, bombed-out building as being questionable.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He successfully sued the newspaper for libel (see below).

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The Christian Science Monitor also published a story on 25 April 2003, stating that it had documentary evidence that Galloway had received "more than ten million dollars" from the Iraqi government.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: However, on 20 June 2003, the Monitor reported that its own investigation had concluded that the documents were sophisticated forgeries.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In January 2004, it was reported that documents from Iraq's oil ministry showed that Galloway's Mariam Appeal received money from businessmen who had had allegedly illicitly siphoned profits from the UN oil-for-food program.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway said that money had been paid into the Mariam Appeal by Iraqi businessmen who had profited from the UN-run programme.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He stated he had not benefited personally and that there was nothing illicit about the transaction:

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: It is hard to see what is dishonourable, let alone "illicit", about Arab nationalist businessmen donating some of the profits they made from legitimate UN-controlled business with Iraq to anti-sanctions campaigns, as opposed to, say, keeping their profits for themselves.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: It's equally difficult to understand why The Guardian should put seven of its finest journalists to work roping Tam Dalyell and Albert Reynolds into the rightwing witch-hunt against me, particularly on the basis of documents that may have been faked or doctored in the forgery capital of the world.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In July 2004, the HM Customs and Excise launched an investigation into the British involvement in alleged corruption related to the oil-for-food programme.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The targets of the investigation were three Middle East businessmen living in Britain, two of whom donated money to the Mariam Appeal, while the third ran Friendship Across Borders for Tam Dalyell.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In May 2005, before the reports by the US Senate and the UN had been published, The Guardian reporter David Pallister wrote that "despite all the investigations in the Oil-for-Food Programme, no one has ever produced any evidence that Iraqi oil money ended up in Mr Galloway's pocket".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In May 2005, a United States Senate committee report accused Galloway and others of receiving, from the Iraqi government, the right to buy oil under the UN's Oil-for-Food Programme.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The report was issued by the US Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, chaired by Senator Norm Coleman, a Republican from Minnesota.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Coleman's committee said that Galloway received oil allocations worth from 2000 to 2003.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The allegations against Galloway, had been made before, including in an October report by US arms inspector Charles Duelfer, as well as in the various purported documents described earlier in this section.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 17 May 2005, the committee held a hearing on allegations that Galloway received illicit payments from the Iraqi government through the Oil-for-Food Program.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Attending Galloway's oral testimony and questioning him were two of the 13 committee members: the chair (Coleman) and the ranking Democrat (Carl Levin).

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On arriving in the US, Galloway told Reuters: "I have no expectation of justice from a group of Christian fundamentalist and Zionist activists."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He described Coleman as a "pro-war, neocon hawk and the lickspittle of George W. Bush", who, he said, sought vengeance against anyone who did not support the war in Iraq.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In his testimony, Galloway made the following statements in response to the allegations against him:

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Senator, I am not now, nor have I ever been, an oil trader—and neither has anyone on my behalf.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: I have never seen a barrel of oil, owned one, bought one, sold one—and neither has anyone on my behalf.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Now I know that standards have slipped in the last few years in Washington, but for a lawyer you are remarkably cavalier with any idea of justice.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: I am here today but last week you already found me guilty.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: You traduced my name around the world without ever having asked me a single question, without ever having contacted me, without ever having written to me or telephoned me, without any attempt to contact me whatsoever, and you call that justice.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway countered the charges by claiming they were politically motivated and a "smokescreen".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He accused Coleman and other pro-war politicians of covering up the "theft of billions of dollars of Iraq's wealth".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He claimed this happened "on your watch" under the post-invasion Coalition Provisional Authority, and was committed by "Halliburton and other American corporations... with the connivance of your own government".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The report, by the then-majority Republican Party staff of the Senate committee, was published in October 2005.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: It stated that Galloway had "knowingly made false or misleading statements under oath".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The report exhibits bank statements, which the authors claim show that $150,000 of proceeds from the Oil-for-Food Program had been paid to Galloway's wife Amineh Abu-Zayyad.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: It also stated that Galloway (and the Mariam Appeal) received eight allocations of oil from the Iraqi government amounting to 23 million barrels from 1999 to 2003.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The Mariam Appeal was also found to have improperly received $446,000 via the Oil-for-Food Program.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Iraq's former prime minister Tariq Aziz was said to have told the investigators that oil had been allocated in the names of two of Galloway's representatives: Buhan Al-Chalabi and Fawaz Zureikat.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Aziz had told the investigators: "These oil allocations were for the benefit of George Galloway and for Mariam's Appeal.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The proceeds from the sale benefited the cause and Mr Galloway".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway reiterated his denial of the charges and asked the US Senate committee to charge him with perjury so that he could confront the charges in court.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He said the investigation was an attempt to divert attention from the "pack of lies" that led to the Iraq invasion in 2003.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He said Coleman's motive was revenge over the embarrassment of his appearance before the committee in May.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway also said he spoke to Aziz's lawyers, who told him "Tariq Aziz absolutely denies ever saying that I benefited from oil deals".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The United Nations (UN) had set up its own committee, the 'Paul Volcker Committee', to investigate alleged corruption in the Oil-for-Food program.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In its October 2005 report, it stated that "over 18 million barrels of oil were allocated either directly in the name of George Galloway ... or in the name of one of his associates, Fawaz Abdullah Zureikat, to support Mr Galloway's campaign against sanctions ...

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Zureikat received commissions for handling the sale of approximately 11 million barrels that were allocated in Mr Galloway's name".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The report further holds that: "Iraq officials identified Mr Zureikat as acting on Mr Galloway's behalf to conduct the oil transactions in Baghdad".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The report states that payments of $445,000 were channelled through Galloway's Mariam Appeal, and claims that $120,000 from oil sales was paid into the bank account of Galloway's wife Amineh Abu Zayyad, who was also involved with the Mariam Appeal.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The committee chairman, Paul Volcker, suggested that his investigation had further material about Galloway which had not been published.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He said "If the legal authorities in Britain want to discuss with us what other evidence we may have, that may not be in the report, then we would be prepared to co-operate".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: However, the committee did not show evidence that any of the money was paid directly into accounts held by George Galloway.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The report acknowledges that "both Mr Galloway and Mr Zureikat have denied that Mr Galloway was involved in obtaining the oil allocations or receiving any proceeds from the oil sales".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway wrote to the committee saying: "I had nothing to do with any oil deals done by Mr Fawaz Zureikat or anyone else.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He and any other company involved were trading on their own behalf".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Aziz was also interviewed for the Volcker Committee, but changed his story, which the committee considered unconvincing.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: When the allegations against Galloway emerged in 2003, the UK parliament's Commissioner for Standards began investigating, as Galloway was a Member of Parliament and none of the alleged funding had been declared in the Register of Members' Interests.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The Commissioner, Philip Mawer, was overseen by the Standards and Privileges Committee.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: After a four-year investigation, he published a detailed report in 2007, which concluded:

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: I have not found a "smoking gun" which shows that Mr Galloway has, personally and directly, unlawfully received moneys from the former Iraqi regime.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: However I have amassed a very substantial body of evidence from a variety of sources which is generally internally consistent and, in my view:

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: a) Clearly shows that Mr Galloway's anti-sanctions work through the Mariam Appeal was in effect supported by the former Iraqi regime, through Mr Fawaz Zureikat and using, among other things, the mechanism of the Oil for Food Programme.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: b) Clearly shows that Mr Galloway at best turned a blind eye to the fact that this was happening.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: c) Shows that it is more likely than not that Mr Galloway knew about and was complicit in what was happening.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The Commissioner stated that he did not have "access to bank accounts held either solely by Mr Galloway or jointly by him with others".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway wrote in an article for The Guardian at the end of October 2003 that he would soon be part of a coalition consisting of the "red, green, anti-war, Muslim and other social constituencies radicalised by the war."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In January 2004, it emerged that Galloway would be working with the Socialist Workers Party in England and Wales, and others, under the name Respect – The Unity Coalition, generally referred to simply as "Respect".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In the opinion of Nick Cohen of The Observer it was an "alliance... between the Trotskyist far left and the Islamic far right."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway announced in December 2003 that he would not force a by-election and did not intend to contest the next general election in Glasgow.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: His Glasgow Kelvin seat was to be split between three constituencies for the next general election.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In one of these, the new Glasgow Central constituency, Mohammad Sarwar, the first Muslim Labour MP, wanted to be selected as the candidate.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway chose not to challenge him, announcing this decision at the end of May 2004 in his Mail on Sunday column.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: After the 2004 European Parliamentary election results became known, in which Galloway stood in London, but did not gain a seat, he announced that he would stand in East London at the next general election.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 2 December, he confirmed that he was aiming to be nominated as the Respect Party candidate for Bethnal Green and Bow.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The ensuing electoral campaign in the seat proved to be a difficult one with heated exchanges between Galloway, Oona King (the incumbent Labour MP for Bethnal Green and Bow), and their respective supporters.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway and Respect threatened to sue King, whose mother is Jewish, if she repeated her assertion in the Evening Standard on 10 April 2005 which reported her as saying: "I have been told by several people that members of Respect have told Muslim voters 'not to vote for me because I am Jewish.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: A major issue of the campaign was King's support for the Iraq War.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway was asked at a hustings early in the campaign why he was standing against one of only two black female MPs to which he replied that King had "voted to kill a lot of women in the last few years.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Many of them had much darker skins than her".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Claiming to be the ghost of Old Labour, Galloway told The Sunday Times contributor A. A. Gill that "we're here to haunt new Labour".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Bethnal Green and Bow is "where Labour was founded.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: We're giving birth to the Labour Party all over again".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway said at a hustings event that the Labour Government had been pursuing a "war on Muslims" while King said her stance against Saddam Hussein had been "principled".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway received death threats from an offshoot of al-Muhajiroun (a banned extreme Islamist group).

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 19 April, about 30 men forced Galloway's meeting with a tenants' association to be abandoned after claiming he was a "false prophet" for encouraging Muslims to vote.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway was held by the group for about 20 minutes before the police arrived at the scene.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: All the major candidates united in condemning the threats and violence.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Both the Labour and Respect candidates were given police protection.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: It emerged in a Channel 4 Dispatches programme in 2010 that the Islamic Forum of Europe, which advocates sharia law, had been involved in campaigning for Galloway in the Bethnal Green constituency.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In a secretly recorded speech at a dinner shortly after his election, Galloway said that the involvement of the IFE had played "the decisive role" in his win.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Although the IFE itself denied the accusation, Galloway admitted in a statement that the allegation was true.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 5 May, Galloway gained the seat from the Labour Party with a narrow majority of 823 votes, and denounced the returning officer for alleged discrepancies in the electoral process.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He was reported to have exploited the generational gap and garnered the support of young Muslim voters.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: After the election result became known, Galloway's spokesman, Ron McKay, rejected claims that King had been racially abused during the campaign and said it was King who had brought up her Jewish background.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In his acceptance speech, Galloway said "Mr Blair, this is for Iraq".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: During the BBC's election night coverage, Jeremy Paxman asked Galloway about whether he was happy to have removed one of the few black women in parliament, He replied: "I don't believe that people get elected because of the colour of their skin.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: I believe that people get elected because of their record and because of their policies".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Oona King later told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that she found Paxman's line of questioning inappropriate.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway "shouldn't be barred from running against me because I'm a black woman....

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: I was not defined, or did not wish to be defined, by either my ethnicity or religious background".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In January 2006, Galloway appeared on the fourth series of the reality TV programme Celebrity Big Brother for nearly three weeks.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: During his time on the programme, he mimed licking imaginary milk, whilst pretending to be a cat, from the cupped hands of another housemate, actress Rula Lenska.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He wrote later that his activities "were actually the same stunts that BBC presenters and celebs get up for Children in Need".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway faced a claim at the time from Hilary Armstrong, Labour's Chief Whip, that he should "respect his constituents, not his ego".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Ron McKay, his spokesman and friend, said of the imaginary milk incident: "I rather wish he hadn't been given that particularly silly task".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: It had been assumed, McKay said, that Galloway's comments about politics would not be cut.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Just after his eviction, Galloway told presenter Davina McCall he was positive about having taken part, although when asked if he was "glad" to have participated, he said: "Not after I've seen those press cuttings."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway wrote in a column for The Independent newspaper in November 2012 that his "antics on Big Brother" had "raised tens of thousands of pounds for the charity Interpal" and paid for an "extra caseworker in my constituency".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 17 July 2007, following a four-year inquiry, the House of Commons Select Committee on Standards and Privileges published its sixth report.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards, in an addendum to the report, concluded that there was no evidence that Galloway gained any personal benefit from either the former Iraqi administration, or from the Oil-for-Food Programme, but admitted that some documents had been unavailable to him.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: However, the Committee concluded, in the main body of the report:

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: we agree with the Commissioner that there is strong circumstantial evidence that the Oil for Food Programme was used by the Iraqi government, with Mr Galloway's connivance, to fund the campaigning activities of the Mariam Appeal.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: It found that Galloway's use of parliamentary resources to support his work on the Mariam Appeal "went beyond what was reasonable" and "we recommend that he apologise to the House, and be suspended from its service for a period of 18 actual sitting days."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway's suspension was not intended to be immediate, and he was given the opportunity to defend himself in front of the committee members in the House of Commons on 23 July 2007.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: During the debate, Galloway repeatedly called into question the motives of the members of the Select Committee, in particular alleging that some of them were members of a political organisation named "Indict" and were persecuting him for speaking out against the Iraq War.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Speaker Michael Martin warned Galloway that his accusations were not relevant to the matter at hand, but he rejected the warning and responded by saying that Martin would have to order him out of the house if he had any issue with the accusations.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
