sentences.text: Galloway has worked for the Iranian state-run satellite television channel, Press TV since 2008.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: During an event at the London School of Economics in March 2011, he said: "Because I don't believe that the government of Iran is a dictatorship I have no problem about working for Press TV in London which is a British owned television station.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: I'm not responsible for the government of Ahmedinejad.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: I'm not responsible for the leadership of Press TV".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway also said: "There are many things wrong with Iran.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: One thing they do have is elections.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: They elected a president that you or I might not have voted for but I am in no doubt that Ahmadinejad won the presidential election" held in 2009.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: (See Television presenter below.)

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In March 2008, Galloway said that the issue of gay rights in Iran was being misused by supporters of war against Iran.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He said on The Wright Stuff chat show that the executed boyfriend of gay Iranian asylum seeker Mehdi Kazemi was executed for "sex crimes" rather than for being gay.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Scott Long, writing in The Guardian on 31 March, criticised Galloway's claim that "homosexuals are not executed in Iran, just rapists," pointing out that current law in the country stipulates that "Penetrative sex acts between men can bring death on the first conviction."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Gay rights activist Peter Tatchell, writing in The Guardian on 26 March, wrote that Galloway's "passionate opposition to a war against Iran, which I share, seems to have clouded his judgement" and "his claim that lesbian and gay people are not at risk of execution in Iran is refuted by every reputable human rights organisation, including Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, the International Gay and Lesbian Human Rights Commission and the International Lesbian and Gay Association".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In August 2010, on his Press TV programme The Real Deal, Galloway interviewed President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, following Galloway's participation in a conference for expatriate Iranians whose expenses were paid by Iran's government.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He discussed Sakineh Mohammadi Ashtiani, an Iranian woman convicted of adultery and sentenced to stoning, which he described as "the so-called stoning case".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway said of Ashtiani's sentence: "Every so often an issue comes along which is seized upon by the enemies of Iran and it becomes a heavy problem and magnified...".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: According to Martin Fletcher in The Times, Ahmadinejad gave "mendacious answers" which "went unchallenged by his obsequious interlocutor".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway told Ahmadinejad: "I have police protection in London from the Iranian opposition because of my support for your election campaign" in 2009.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: "I mention this so you know where I'm coming from."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In May 2025, Galloway was awarded the Ismail Haniyeh Prize at the Iranian state-organized Sobh International Media Festival, named after the assassinated former chairman of Hamas.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In his acceptance speech, he praised Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, stating: "I thank the revolutionary people of Iran, your leadership, your heroes, and your martyrs for standing firm in support of the Palestinian people."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway had long supported devolution for Scotland, but opposed Scottish independence.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In the run-up to the Scottish independence referendum, held on 18 September 2014, Galloway was dismissive of the official Better Together campaign because it also involved Conservatives and Liberal Democrats, and he believed its leader, Alistair Darling, to be ineffective.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: "My case isn't that Scotland couldn't be independent, but shouldn't", The Sunday Times quoted him as saying.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He was among 200 public figures to sign a letter to The Guardian opposing independence in the run up to the referendum.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway's argument against independence was based on "class" over "nationality".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He told Serena Kutchinsky in an interview for Prospect magazine: "If we lose this vote the possibility of a real Labour government, or any kind of Labour government, in the rest of UK will be gone".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In 2013, Galloway began a series of public meetings in Scotland, using the slogan "Just Say Naw" to independence.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 11 September 2014, Galloway took part in Scotland Decides: The Big, Big Debate, an independence debate held in Glasgow and broadcast by the BBC during the evening.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In July 2020, Galloway co-founded and established a cross-party Scottish unionist political coalition called Alliance 4 Unity (later re-named All for Unity).

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Its goal was to defeat the Scottish National Party and Scottish nationalism in general at the 2021 Scottish Parliament election, by tactical voting for any Scottish unionist candidates in the proportional vote on each Scottish electoral regions.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: During the election campaign Galloway was criticised for "race-baiting" comments about the then Cabinet Secretary for Justice Humza Yousaf, about who he tweeted "Well #Humza you're not more Scottish than me.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: You're not a Celt like me."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In June 2025, Galloway announced his support for a second referendum, adding that it is the 'right of Scots to self-determination.'

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In March 2026, Galloway announced his shift to support Scottish independence.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In 2014, Galloway said he would "be campaigning to remain in the European Union, as anyone with any brain cells will also be doing".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: However, in 2016, he began campaigning for the UK to leave the EU.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: At a rally at the Queen Elizabeth II Conference Centre on 19 February 2016, Galloway endorsed the Grassroots Out (GO) campaign for the European Union membership referendum.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He was introduced by UKIP leader Nigel Farage as a "special guest" who is "without doubt one of the greatest orators in this country, he is a towering figure on the left of British politics".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway's presence at the rally prompted some of those present to leave.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Labour MP Kate Hoey, who was involved with GO, defended Galloway's participation.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: "George ended up getting a hugely favourable response to what he said".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Responding to criticism of his association with Farage, Galloway tweeted: "We are not pals.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: We are allies in one cause.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Like Churchill and Stalin".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 17 April 2019 Galloway announced he would support the Brexit Party led by Nigel Farage in the May 2019 European Parliament election.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He said that "given the nature of Labour's Euro-fanatic candidates list and the crucial juncture we have reached in the fight for the full implementation of the Brexit referendum result and for one-time only I will be supporting Nigel Farage in next months elections."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: From 2013 to 2022 Galloway was a presenter on the Russian state-controlled television network RT.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway called the 2014 Ukrainian Revolution a Western-backed "coup" and a "foreign financed invasion of the sovereignty of Ukraine".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He believes Russia's annexation of Crimea was legitimate, because he said the disputed 2014 Crimean status referendum showed that "the huge majority of people in Crimea wanted to leave Ukraine".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In a 2016 interview of Nigel Farage, Galloway said "I respect Putin and I think he's very popular in Russia".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: When Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny was poisoned in August 2020, Galloway claimed on RT that Navalny was a white supremacist.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In early 2022, Galloway dismissed claims that Russia was about to invade Ukraine, writing "I told you it wasn't. You were wrong.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: I was right".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: When Russia invaded Ukraine ten days later, he said the invasion was "not what I wanted", but he blamed the invasion on "the West" and accused it of "Pumping Ukraine full of NATO weapons, mercenaries and propaganda".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He suggested that the Bucha massacre was staged.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway was accused of being an apologist and propagandist for Russian president Vladimir Putin by the larger political parties.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Jamie Blackett ended their political alliance All for Unity over their disagreement on Ukraine.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The Scottish Liberal Democrats leader, Alex Cole-Hamilton, called Galloway "an apologist for Russian expansionist aggression" and said that Galloway's "association with RT has lent legitimacy and influence to the propaganda apparatus of a hostile power".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In October 2023, Galloway promoted the false claim that Volodymyr Zelenskyy's wife Olena Zelenska had spent $1 million on jewelry in New York City, during the time of which Zelenska was actually in Canada.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway said that his source for the story was The Nation, but the publication that had actually reported this claim was a Nigerian newspaper of the same name.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Regarding the Crocus City Hall attack in Russia, Galloway said he had "four pieces of evidence that lead [him] to believe that the United States, its NATO allies, and their puppet stump state Ukraine are, in fact, responsible for this massacre".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In October 2024, at the 16th BRICS summit, Galloway criticised the British press at the event for "hating Russia" and suggested there was more media freedom in Russia than in Britain.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In June 2025, Galloway participated as a speaker at the Forum of the Future 2050 in Moscow, a conference organised by tycoon Konstantin Malofeev.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The guest list also included Elon Musk's father, Errol Musk, Russia's foreign minister Sergey Lavrov, economist Jeffrey Sachs and conspiracy theorist Alex Jones, among others.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: After going into self-imposed exile in Russia, Galloway said on his talk show that he supports Russia's war against Ukraine, calling it anti-imperialist and anti-colonialist.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He praised Russia's military after it struck Yahodyn, on the Polish border, with a drone.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In 2019, Galloway defended the authorities' crackdown on protests in Hong Kong.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He told China Global Television Network: "These people should know that Hong Kong is China.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: No country, absolutely no country, will allow an existential threat to emerge on its territory".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In 2022, he said there were no internment camps for Uighurs in China.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He stated that China had established "re-education centres" to steer terrorists away from the path of extremism.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway said, after spending time in North Korea, he "does not agree with the North Korean system" and would not like to live there.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He said "there have been achievements in North Korea ...

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: They have a cohesive, pristine actually, innocent culture, a culture not penetrated by globalisation and Western mores".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: During a period of tension between North and South Korea in 2013, Galloway said "North Korea has no intention to harm any of us.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: North Korea's problem is with South Korea.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: South Korea exists because America invaded Korea, killed millions of people, divided the country and continues to garrison South Korea with military bases, nuclear weapons, chemical and biological weapon".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He blamed the United States for "war mongering" during the crisis and called South Korea its "puppet state".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He has been an advocate for the Venezuelan government of Hugo Chávez and, in his Fidel Castro Handbook, for the former Cuban leader.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: "You were the greatest man I ever met Comandante Fidel.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: You were the man of the century", he tweeted when Castro died in November 2016.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway has criticised Britain's close ties with Saudi Arabia and British involvement in the Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In 2017, he said: "It is a country with no democracy or freedom of any kind.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: It is a country that exports terrorism around the world and funds terrorism and extremism around the world.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: We should have nothing whatsoever to do with them."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway opposes India's role in the Kashmir conflict with Pakistan, and has voiced support for the insurgency in Indian-administered Kashmir.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He said the Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi "has blood on his hands".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Modi was accused of initiating and condoning the 2002 Gujarat riots against India's Muslim minority.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In October 1991, Galloway tabled a motion in the House of Commons expressing concern at the allegations against news publisher Mirror Group Newspapers put forward in Seymour Hersh's recently published book, The Samson Option: Israel's Nuclear Arsenal and American Foreign Policy.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Hersh alleged that the Daily Mirror's foreign editor, Nicholas Davies, was involved in weapons sales to Iran and had given the whereabouts of Mordechai Vanunu to Mossad.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Mossad sought to capture Vanunu due to his role as a whistleblower of Israeli nuclear operations, and later "lured [him] out of Britain to Italy", where he "was kidnapped, drugged and returned to Israel".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway's motion also called upon Mirror Group's owner, Robert Maxwell, to appoint a tribunal to investigate the allegations and the potential involvement of foreign intelligence in the publishing group.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: As the motion was signed under parliamentary privilege, other news outlets could report on it without worrying about legal repercussion, as Maxwell was known for litigiousness.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Following this, the Daily Mirror published a "vitriolic" front-page editorial against Galloway, accusing him of abusing parliamentary privilege and of being motivated by links to anti-Israel terrorist groups.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway sued for libel and was awarded a public apology and substantial undisclosed damages from the Mirror Group.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 22 April 2003, The Daily Telegraph published news articles and comment describing documents found by its reporter David Blair in the ruins of the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The documents purported to be records of meetings between Galloway and Iraqi intelligence agents, and they stated that he had received £375,000 per year from the proceeds of the Oil-for-Food Programme.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway sued the newspaper for libel by November 2003, and the case was heard in the High Court on 14 November 2004.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 2 December, Justice David Eady ruled that the story had been "seriously defamatory", and that The Daily Telegraph was "obliged to compensate Mr Galloway... and to make an award for the purposes of restoring his reputation."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway was awarded damages of £150,000 plus, after a failed appeal in 2006, legal costs of about £2 million.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Both sides regarded the libel case as an important test of the Reynolds qualified-privilege defence.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The Daily Telegraph did not attempt to claim justification (where the defendant seeks to prove the truth of the defamatory reports): "It has never been the Telegraph case to suggest that the allegations contained in these documents are true".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The newspaper argued that it acted responsibly as the allegations it reported were of sufficient public interest to outweigh the damage caused to Galloway's reputation.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The trial judge did not accept this defence, noting that comments such as Galloway being guilty of "treason", "in Saddam's pay", and being "Saddam's little helper" caused him [the judge] to conclude that "the newspaper was not neutral but both embraced the allegations with relish and fervour and went on to embellish them"; additionally, the judge ruled, Galloway had not been given a fair or reasonable opportunity to make inquiries or meaningful comment upon the documents before they were published.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The Christian Science Monitor also published a story on 25 April 2003, stating that it had documentary evidence that he had received "more than ten million dollars" from the Iraqi government.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 20 June 2003, the Monitor reported that its own investigation had concluded that the documents were sophisticated forgeries.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway sued The Christian Science Monitor for libel.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In March 2004, he accepted damages and a public apology from the Monitor.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In November 2007, Jewish radio station Jcom aired a satirical segment in which a character named 'Georgie Galloway' used the anti-Semitic catchphrase "kill the Jews, kill the Jews".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway sued the station for libel and won the case in the High Court.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway was awarded £15,000 in damages and around £5,000 in costs.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The radio station closed after losing the case.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway said the judgment had "categorically crushed the slur of anti-Semitism" against him.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 5 February 2015, Galloway appeared on BBC's Question Time discussion programme, recorded in Finchley, London, within a constituency with Britain's largest Jewish community.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The Jewish Chronicle wrote that "Galloway was heckled by Jewish audience members who challenged him on his anti-Israel record" and the audience shouted "You're not welcome here".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Five days later, Hadley Freeman, a columnist for The Guardian, tweeted: "Galloway has said and done things that cross the line from anti-Israel to antisemitic".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway said that he would issue a suit for defamation against her.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Freeman then deleted the tweet.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Some who had re-tweeted Freeman's comment were then sent a letter from Chambers Solicitors, acting for Galloway, asking for an apology and £5,000 plus Value Added Tax (then levied at 20%) to cover costs incurred by the letter.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Some people who received the letter complained to the Solicitors Regulation Authority.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Eric Heinze, Professor of Law at Queen Mary University of London, noted that an editor of the Media Lens website had sent a tweet to Freeman asking if she could provide evidence for her claim that Galloway is antisemitic.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Heinze wrote that "any example she could cite would probably persuade some and not others.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Even if an overwhelming majority were unpersuaded, a highly popular opinion does not create an objectively verifiable fact."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Chambers Solicitors' conduct was the subject of a warning from the SRA a year later.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Initiating a libel action must begin within a year and no formal writ was issued.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: On 20 June 2016, Galloway lost a libel action brought by Aisha Ali-Khan, his assistant for six months in 2012.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He had claimed that she had pursued a "dirty tricks" campaign against him and the Respect Party, and had slept at his house with her then-husband.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The case was heard in the High Court.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: His counsel apologised on Galloway's behalf, and accepted that he had made "defamatory accusations".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Ali-Khan will receive a "five-figure sum" in damages and her legal costs.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: As part of the settlement of their libel claim, both Galloway and Ali-Khan gave undertakings not to make any further public statement about the litigation or to defame each other.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In 2018 Galloway brought an action that Ali-Khan had breached this undertaking 26 times, which Ali-Khan admitted, and in April 2018 the High Court imprisoned Ali-Khan for 12 weeks for contempt of court, describing her action as "deliberate, flagrant, persistent and inexcusable".

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Ali-Khan had been found guilty of contempt of court on a previous occasion.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Previously, during 2017, Ali-Khan had filed a petition for Galloway's bankruptcy.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In April 2022, Galloway's Twitter account was labelled "Russian state-affiliated media" by Twitter.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In response Galloway tweeted: "I work for NO Russian media.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: I have 400,000 followers.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: I'm the leader of a British political party and spent nearly 30 years in the British parliament.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: If you do not remove this designation I will take legal action."

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Twitter users pointed out that Galloway's profile named the Russian state media outlets that he worked for.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway then removed these from his profile.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: He said Twitter had refused to explain the label, which he said was added to his account after he had stopped presenting on Russian television channels, which were closed by the British government in March 2022.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: Galloway sued Twitter for defamation in the High Court, Dublin.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: The suit also alleged that Twitter had unlawfully processed his personal data by labelling and censoring his account.

sentences.section: MP for Glasgow Hillhead and Kelvin (1987–2005)
sentences.text: In October 2024, the High Court in Dublin ordered Twitter to pay Galloway's legal costs.
